userStories.title: Thread stream acceptance, read refusal, append hook and schema
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make the API accept the `thread` log stream for THREAD jobs, hide it from every job-log read route and live event, add a post-append `LogAppendHooks` extension point, and land the schema/migration and test fixtures that the fold stories build on.

**Motivation** — The API refuses the runner's `thread` stream today with 400 `fleet.logInput`, so no reply ever reaches a thread.

**Approach** (verbatim from spec)
- `isLogStream` / `LOG_STREAMS` (`apps/api/src/fleet/logs/domain/fleet-job-log.domain.ts:1-6`): unchanged (readable streams `['run','stdout','stderr']`); the file gains `UPLOAD_STREAMS = [...LOG_STREAMS, 'thread']` and `isUploadStream(value)`.
- `logKey(jobId, leaseEpoch, stream)` (`log-store.ts:28-33`): `stream: UploadStreamName`; throws unless `isUploadStream(stream)`; `logKey('j1', 1, 'thread')` = `logs/j1/1/thread.log`.
- `FleetJobLogRecord.stream`, `IFleetJobLogRepository.findStream` / `upsertStream` and `PrismaFleetJobLogRepository`: `UploadStreamName` (`LogStreamName | 'thread'`); `FleetLogLivePublisher.touch`, `LogReadService` and `LiveFleetLogEvent.stream` keep the narrow `LogStreamName`: `LogReadService` narrows rows with `isLogStream` (which also drops `thread`), and `LogFallbackService` already iterates `LOG_STREAMS` only; the `FleetJobLog.stream` schema comment gains `thread`.
- `LogUploadService.parse` (`log-upload.service.ts:125-133`): `isUploadStream`; then, in `upload`, a `thread` stream for a job whose `command` is not `THREAD` -> 400 `fleet.logInput` (`reason: 'stream'`).
- `LogUploadService.upload` (`:70-93`): skips `live.touch` for `thread`; after the lock is released, for the outcomes `appended`, `complete` and `stream_cap`, awaits `LogAppendHooks.run({ jobId, leaseEpoch, stream })`, catching and logging a hook failure.
- `LogUploadService` constructor: an optional 8th parameter, `@Optional() hooks?: LogAppendHooks` (positional spec construction keeps compiling).
- `LogsModule` provides and exports `LogAppendHooks`.
- `LogReadService.target` / `list` (`log-read.service.ts:91-154`): unknown stream names -> 400 unchanged; `thread` -> 404 `fleet.logs`; `list` drops `thread` rows before building attempts, so an epoch whose only row is `thread` (and that has no log events) is not listed.
- Raw `thread` stream is never served by the job-log routes: no `fleet_log` live event is published for it.

**Upload hook**: `LogAppendHooks` (`apps/api/src/fleet/logs/log-append-hooks.ts`): `register(stream: string, hook: (e: { jobId: string; leaseEpoch: number; stream: string }) => Promise<void>): void` and `run(e): Promise<void>`, which awaits every hook registered for `e.stream` in registration order. `LogUploadService.upload` calls `run` after `store.withLock(...)` has returned (never inside it: the hook takes the same lock) and only for the outcomes `appended`, `complete` and `stream_cap`. A hook that rejects is logged with the job id and swallowed; the upload result is unchanged.

**Data**
```prisma
/// Durable fold position of one THREAD job attempt's `thread` stream.
model ThreadIngestCursor {
  jobId        String
  leaseEpoch   Int
  offset       BigInt   @default(0)   // bytes folded; always at a line boundary
  skippedLines Int      @default(0)   // bad or unknown lines passed over
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt
  job          FleetJob @relation(fields: [jobId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  @@id([jobId, leaseEpoch])
}
```
`ChatThread.session Json?`; `ChatMessage.streamRound Int?`, `ChatMessage.streamRoundStart Int?`. Migration `apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261014090000_thread_ingest/migration.sql`. No partial index. Add the `FleetJob` back-relation.

**Test fixtures** `apps/api/test/helpers/thread-fixtures.ts`: `seedThreadJob` (a thread, a RUNNING THREAD job held by an enrolled runner at epoch 1 with `firstStartedAt` set, its `FleetThreadTurn`, optional `pending` user messages) and `putThreadLines(server, runnerKey, job, lines, offset?)` (JSONL body, SHA-256 header; returns the new size). Seed defaults: thread T of the `web` project, created by `dev`, backend `{ kind: 'native', model: 'm1' }`, feature `add-auth`; THREAD job J RUNNING on enrolled runner R at lease epoch 1; `FleetThreadTurn.resume` false.

**Scope** — In: stream acceptance and refusal rules, LogAppendHooks, schema+migration, fixtures. Out: any folding of lines (US-002+), ThreadIngestModule and the ingestor (US-002), `ThreadSession` DTO exposure (US-004).

**Interface**
```typescript
type UploadStreamName = LogStreamName | 'thread';
const UPLOAD_STREAMS: readonly UploadStreamName[];
function isUploadStream(value: unknown): value is UploadStreamName;
class LogAppendHooks {
  register(stream: string, hook: (e: { jobId: string; leaseEpoch: number; stream: string }) => Promise<void>): void;
  run(e: { jobId: string; leaseEpoch: number; stream: string }): Promise<void>;
}
```
acceptanceCriteria: logKey('j1', 1, 'thread') from log-store.ts returns 'logs/j1/1/thread.log'
isLogStream('thread') from fleet-job-log.domain.ts returns false

PUT /api/fleet/runner/jobs/J/logs/thread?leaseEpoch=1&offset=0 by runner R with a 40-byte JSONL body answers 200 with { outcome: 'appended', size: 40 }, and the FleetJobLog row for (J, 1, 'thread') has sizeBytes 40
The same PUT for a RUNNING RUN job held by R answers 400 with the fleet.logInput message
After a thread upload for J, GET /api/projects/web/fleet/jobs/J/logs by dev answers 200 and lists no stream named 'thread'
GET /api/projects/web/fleet/jobs/J/logs/thread/entries?leaseEpoch=1 by dev answers 404 with the fleet.logs message

With a listener subscribed through app.get(ProjectEventBus).subscribe(projectId, ...), an appended thread upload for J followed by an appended run upload for a RUN job of the same project delivers a fleet_log event for the RUN job and none for J
LogAppendHooks with a hook registered for 'thread': run({ jobId: 'j1', leaseEpoch: 1, stream: 'thread' }) calls the hook once with that object

LogUploadService constructed with a LogAppendHooks holding a 'thread' hook: an upload that appends to stream 'thread' of a THREAD job calls the hook once with { jobId, leaseEpoch: 1, stream: 'thread' }
LogUploadService: repeating an identical thread upload (outcome 'duplicate') does not call the hook again
LogUploadService with a 'thread' hook that rejects: the upload resolves { outcome: 'appended', size } with the appended size
LogUploadService with a 'thread' hook that calls store.withLock(logKey(jobId, 1, 'thread'), ...): the upload resolves (the hook runs after the write lock is released)
Inserting a second ThreadIngestCursor row with the same jobId and leaseEpoch fails with a unique-constraint violation
Deleting a FleetJob row deletes its ThreadIngestCursor rows
Applying the 20261014090000_thread_ingest migration with applyMigration to a scratch schema from scratchSchemaBefore that holds one ChatThread row leaves that row with session null

routing.reasoning: Several existing files widened with a new stream type, a new small hook class, schema+migration; standard patterns, no new abstraction beyond LogAppendHooks.

suggestedCriteria: LogReadService.list omits an epoch whose only FleetJobLog row is 'thread' and that has no log events
LogUploadService.upload does not call live.touch for stream 'thread'
A PUT to an unknown stream name such as 'bogus' still answers 400 fleet.logInput
An appended run-stream upload for a RUN job still publishes a fleet_log event and does not invoke any thread hook
outOfScope: Folding of thread lines into rows (US-002 onward)
US-001 only: `GET .../logs/thread/raw` and the download route share the `thread` refusal of the entries route; only entries is pinned.

modifiedFiles.reason: gains `ThreadIngestCursor` (with the `FleetJob` back-relation), `ChatThread.session`, `ChatMessage.streamRound` and `ChatMessage.streamRoundStart`; integration suites build their schema from this file.

userStories.title: Thread ingestor engine: cursor, batches, bad lines
acceptanceCriteria: With vi.spyOn(app.get(ThreadIngestor), 'catchUp'), a thread PUT for J calls catchUp with ('J', 1)
Putting the line { type: 'input_consumed', messageId: M1 } sets M1's status to 'complete', and the ThreadIngestCursor for (J, 1) has offset equal to the stream size
Putting input_consumed with the id of a user message of another thread leaves that message unchanged and sets the cursor's skippedLines to 1

A PUT whose body is the input_consumed line for M1 followed by the first half of the input_consumed line for M2 (no newline) sets M1 complete, leaves M2 pending and leaves the cursor at the end of the M1 line; a following PUT with the rest of the M2 line sets M2 complete
A PUT of three lines, input_consumed M1, the text 'not json', and input_consumed M2, sets M1 and M2 complete and skippedLines to 1
Putting a line { type: 'foo' } sets skippedLines to 1
Putting a line { type: 'thinking_delta', turnId: 't1', round: 1, text: 'x' } leaves skippedLines 0
A PUT of input_consumed M1, a 70 000-byte line (input_consumed M2 with a 70 000-character extra pad field), and nothing else sets M1 complete, leaves M2 pending and sets skippedLines to 1

With FLEET_LOG_SCAN_BYTES=65536, a PUT of three input_consumed lines for M1, M2 and a third pending message M3, each padded with a 30 000-character extra pad field, sets all three messages complete and the cursor offset to the stream size

ThreadIngestor.catchUp over a fake ThreadIngestRepository whose fold rejects any batch containing the second of three lines: the first and third lines are folded, the second is folded as a bad line (skippedLines 1), and the final cursor offset is the end of the third line
parseThreadLine for the bytes of {"type":"input_consumed","messageId":"m1"} returns a line of type 'input_consumed' with messageId 'm1'
parseThreadLine for {"type":"input_consumed","messageId":7} returns { bad: true }
The API's THREAD_STREAM_LIMITS from thread-jobs.ts deep-equals the package's THREAD_STREAM_LIMITS (runtime import in the spec), which is { lineMaxBytes: 65536, streamMaxBytes: 209715200 }

routing.reasoning: New abstractions (ingestor, parser, repository, module), transactional exactly-once cursor, lock ordering, failure isolation, non-reentrant mutex constraints.

suggestedCriteria: parseThreadLine returns { ignored: true } for types thinking_delta, compaction and tool_progress
catchUp on a job whose command is not THREAD folds nothing and creates no cursor
ThreadIngestModule.onModuleInit registers a 'thread' hook with LogAppendHooks that invokes ThreadIngestor.catchUp
outOfScope: Assistant message, tool, question, session and cost line effects (US-003 to US-005)

US-002 only: two catch-ups of one stream are serialized by the stream's `withLock` key and the fold transaction locks the job row, then the thread row (B1 order); no acceptance criterion races two uploads or an upload against a job end.
US-002 only: per-type length bounds (`turnId`, `messageId`, `callId`, `name`, `requestId`, `reason`, `decidedBy`) share the line validation without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

modifiedFiles.reason: gains a parity case: the API's `THREAD_STREAM` and `THREAD_STREAM_LIMITS` deep-equal the package's (runtime import in the spec), because the mirror gained the stream constants. Existing parity assertions unchanged.

userStories.title: Assistant message lifecycle
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fold `turn_start`, `text_delta`, `stream_reset` and `turn_end` into the assistant `ChatMessage` row, and stop exposing the fold-internal round columns.

**Motivation** — B4's chat page needs the assistant reply as folded rows, streaming in and finalized with the authoritative output.

**Approach** (verbatim from spec)
| type | required fields | fold effect |
| `turn_start` | `turnId` string 1..128 | insert an `assistant` message: `status streaming`, `content ''`, next `seq`, `jobId`, `turnId`; a second `turn_start` with the same `turnId` in the thread -> bad |
| `text_delta` | `turnId`, `round` integer >= 0, `text` string | append `text` to the turn's message content; if `round` differs from `streamRound`, first set `streamRound = round`, `streamRoundStart = content length` |
| `stream_reset` | `turnId`, `round` | if `round === streamRound`, cut content to `streamRoundStart` characters |
| `turn_end` | `turnId`, `status` one of `completed cancelled timed_out interrupted errored`, `output` string, `usage` object with `inputTokens` and `outputTokens` integers >= 0 (optional `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens` integers >= 0, absent read as 0), `costUsd` finite >= 0; optional `costSource`, `error { code?, message? }`, `outputTruncated` | `content = output` when `status` is `completed`, `output !== ''` and `outputTruncated !== true`, else unchanged (whatever the message's status); only when the message is `streaming`: `status` = `complete` for `completed`, else the end status, and `errored` sets `errorReason` = `error.message` (else `error.code`), at most 200 chars. Always: `pendingQuestion` -> null, `lastActivityAt` = fold time, reconcile (US-005) |

A line that names a `turnId` with no assistant message in the thread (other than `turn_start`) is bad. Assistant messages allocate `seq` the same way as `PrismaChatThreadRepository.sendMessage` (`prisma-chat-thread.repository.ts:166`): `UPDATE "ChatThread" SET "nextSeq" = GREATEST(...) + 1 ... RETURNING "nextSeq" - 1`. B2-D2: there is no in-memory delta buffer; each fold transaction writes the content of every message it touched. B2-D1: the fold runs after the upload's write lock is released and before the upload answers; a failing fold never fails the upload. `PrismaChatThreadRepository.messages()` (`:71-73`, maps rows inline today) maps through `mapMessage`, and `mapMessage` (`:260-263`, spreads every column except `threadId`) also leaves out `streamRound` and `streamRoundStart`, so neither the list nor the send result carries them. NUL in string values is replaced with U+FFFD before the fold (US-002 parser).

**Scope** — In: the four lifecycle line effects, line field rules for them, seq allocation, mapMessage/messages() change. Out: tools/questions/session (US-004), usage lines and the turn_end reconcile math (US-005; the `turn_end` fold leaves a reconcile seam), SSE events (US-006).

**Interface**
No new public signatures; extend `ThreadLine` union and `thread-fold.ts` per-line effects. `mapMessage(row)` returns the row without `threadId`, `streamRound`, `streamRoundStart`.
acceptanceCriteria: On a thread whose highest message seq is 1, putting { type: 'turn_start', turnId: 't1' } creates one ChatMessage with role 'assistant', status 'streaming', content '', seq 2, jobId J and turnId 't1'
After turn_start t1, putting text_delta (round 1, text 'Hel') in one PUT and text_delta (round 1, text 'lo') in a second PUT leaves the message's content 'Hello'
After turn_start t1, putting text_delta round 1 'abc', stream_reset round 1 and text_delta round 1 'xyz' leaves content 'xyz'
After turn_start t1, putting text_delta round 1 'one ', text_delta round 2 'two', stream_reset round 2 and text_delta round 2 'TWO' leaves content 'one TWO'
After deltas 'partial', putting turn_end with status 'completed' and output 'Final' sets the message's content to 'Final' and status to 'complete'
After deltas 'partial', putting turn_end with status 'cancelled' and output '' keeps content 'partial' and sets status to 'cancelled'
Putting turn_end with status 'errored', output '' and error: { code: 'E', message: 'boom' } sets status to 'errored' and errorReason to 'boom'
After a PUT that folded turn_start t1 and text_delta 'Hello', calling app.get(ThreadIngestor).catchUp('J', 1) again leaves content 'Hello' and the thread's message count unchanged

After turn_start t1, J is moved to CRASHED (its message becomes errored); then a turn_end line (completed, output 'Late') is appended to J's stored thread stream with LogStore.append and its FleetJobLog sizeBytes updated directly (a PUT would answer 409 for a terminal job), and app.get(ThreadIngestor).catchUp('J', 1) keeps the message 'errored' and sets its content to 'Late'
Putting text_delta for turn 't9', which has no turn_start, creates no message and sets skippedLines to 1
Putting turn_start t1 twice leaves exactly one assistant message with turnId 't1' and skippedLines 1
After turn_start t1, putting text_delta round 1 with text 'a\u0000b' (an escaped NUL in the JSON) sets content to 'a\uFFFDb'
After turn_start t1 and a text_delta, GET /api/projects/web/threads/T/messages by dev answers 200 with items that have neither a streamRound nor a streamRoundStart key
POST /api/projects/web/threads/T/messages by dev answers with a message that has neither a streamRound nor a streamRoundStart key

routing.reasoning: Adds line effects to the fold engine and parser that US-002 already established, plus a small mapMessage change; stateful round handling is local to one module so a single TDD session suffices.

suggestedCriteria: A turn_end with outputTruncated true and status completed keeps the streamed content unchanged
turn_end with errored status and no error.message sets errorReason to error.code truncated to at most 200 characters
turn_end sets the thread's lastActivityAt to the fold time and pendingQuestion to null
outOfScope: Tool, question and session lines (US-004); usage lines and cost reconcile arithmetic (US-005)
US-003 only: `turn_end` with `outputTruncated: true` keeps the streamed text without a dedicated acceptance criterion; it follows the same "content unchanged" rule as a non-completed turn.

userStories.title: Tools, questions and session state
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fold tool, approval, question and session lines; clear the answered `pendingQuestion` on a THREAD_ANSWER ok-ack; serve `session` on `ThreadDto`.

**Motivation** — B4 needs tool chips, question cards and session state, and B1 left `pendingQuestion`/session to B2.

**Approach** (verbatim from spec)
| type | required fields | fold effect |
| `tool_call` | `turnId`, `callId` 1..128, `name` 1..128, `input` any | upsert a `toolSummary` entry |
| `tool_result` | `turnId`, `callId`, `isError` boolean, `preview` string | set the entry's `isError` and `preview` |
| `approval_requested` | `requestId` 1..128; optional `callId` | remember `requestId` on the entry for `callId` |
| `approval_resolved` | `requestId`, `decidedBy` string 1..32 | set `decidedBy` on the entry that holds `requestId` |
| `question` | `turnId`, `requestId`, `text` string, `expiresAt` string that parses as a date; optional `answerable: false` | answerable -> `pendingQuestion = { requestId, text (<= 2048 chars), expiresAt }`; `answerable: false` -> a `toolSummary` entry `{ callId: requestId, name: 'ask_human', preview: text }` |
| `session_started` | `resumed` boolean | `session = { jobId, state: 'live', resumed, contextReset, reason: null, at }` |
| `session_closed` | `reason` string 1..64 | `session.state = 'closed'`, `reason` |
| `session_failed` | `reason` string 1..64 | `session.state = 'failed'`, `reason`; the thread's `pending` and `streaming` messages -> `errored` with `errorReason = reason` (content kept) |

`session_closed` and `session_failed` while `session` is null set `session` with `resumed: false` and `contextReset: false`.

`toolSummary` entry: `{ callId, name, input: string, isError: boolean | null, preview: string, decidedBy: string | null }` (internal `requestId` for approval matching is kept on the entry). `input` is `JSON.stringify(input)` cut to at most 512 UTF-8 bytes on a code point; `preview` is cut the same way. At most 50 entries per message: a `tool_call` for a 51st `callId` is skipped (not counted as bad).

`ThreadSession` (the `session` JSON; `ThreadDto.session`): `{ jobId: string; state: 'live' | 'closed' | 'failed'; resumed: boolean; contextReset: boolean; reason: string | null; at: string }`. `contextReset` is true when the job's `FleetThreadTurn.resume` is true and its `session_started` line says `resumed: false` (the runner lost the transcript). `null` until a thread's first `session_started` is folded. `ChatThreadRecord` and `ThreadDto` gain `session: ThreadSession | null` (with the repository's `mapThread`); `openapi.json` is regenerated by `bun run api:export-spec`.

B2-D3: `pendingQuestion` is cleared when the runner acks the `THREAD_ANSWER` for it with `ok` (B1's ack hook), at the next `turn_end` (US-003), and (already, B1) when the job ends. `ThreadJobEffects.onInputAck` (`thread-job-effects.ts:17`): on `result === 'ok'` for a `THREAD_ANSWER`, reads the command's job (`threadId`; the ack already holds the job lock) and sets that thread's `pendingQuestion` to null when its `requestId` equals the command's `requestId`, before the payload rewrite. A `rejected` ack keeps `pendingQuestion`.

B2-D4: an informational question (`answerable: false`) becomes a `toolSummary` entry named `ask_human`, because `turn_end` replaces a completed message's content with the authoritative output and would erase a note written into it. Lock order for every thread write: job row, then thread row.

**Scope** — In: tool-summary module, question/session/approval fold effects, onInputAck change, ThreadDto.session, openapi regeneration. Out: usage/cost (US-005), SSE (US-006).

**Interface**
```typescript
interface ThreadSession { jobId: string; state: 'live'|'closed'|'failed'; resumed: boolean; contextReset: boolean; reason: string | null; at: string }
interface ToolSummaryEntry { callId: string; name: string; input: string; isError: boolean | null; preview: string; decidedBy: string | null }
// tool-summary.ts: pure functions that return new arrays (immutable), 512-byte code-point-safe cuts, 50-entry cap
```
acceptanceCriteria: After turn_start t1, putting { type: 'tool_call', turnId: 't1', callId: 'c1', name: 'search_repo', input: { pattern: 'foo' } } gives the message a toolSummary deep-equal to [{ callId: 'c1', name: 'search_repo', input: '{"pattern":"foo"}', isError: null, preview: '', decidedBy: null }]
Then putting { type: 'tool_result', turnId: 't1', callId: 'c1', isError: true, preview: 'refused' } sets that entry's isError to true and preview to 'refused'
The tool-summary upsert in tool-summary.ts given a tool_call whose input serializes to 2000 bytes stores an input of at most 512 UTF-8 bytes that is a prefix of the serialization
The tool-summary upsert given a tool_result with a 2000-byte preview stores a preview of at most 512 UTF-8 bytes
Applying 51 tool_calls with distinct callIds to an empty summary leaves 50 entries and no entry for the 51st callId
Putting approval_requested (requestId 'a1', callId 'c1') and then approval_resolved (requestId 'a1', decision 'deny', decidedBy 'profile') sets entry c1's decidedBy to 'profile'

Putting { type: 'question', turnId: 't1', requestId: 'q1', text: 'Which repo?', expiresAt: E } (E an ISO date) sets T's pendingQuestion deep-equal to { requestId: 'q1', text: 'Which repo?', expiresAt: E }
Putting the same question with answerable: false leaves T's pendingQuestion null and adds a toolSummary entry with callId 'q1', name 'ask_human' and preview 'Which repo?'
After an answerable question q1, putting turn_end for t1 sets T's pendingQuestion to null

After an answerable question q1 is folded, POST /api/projects/web/threads/T/answer by dev with { requestId: 'q1', text: 'acme/app' } queues a THREAD_ANSWER command; then POST /api/fleet/runner/sync from R with a commandAcks entry { result: 'ok' } for that command sets T's pendingQuestion to null
The same flow with the ack { result: 'rejected', detail: 'not_pending' } leaves T's pendingQuestion.requestId 'q1'

Putting { type: 'session_started', at: A, resumed: false, backend: { kind: 'native' }, skillShas: [] } sets T's session deep-equal to { jobId: 'J', state: 'live', resumed: false, contextReset: false, reason: null, at: A }
For a THREAD job whose FleetThreadTurn.resume is true, putting session_started with resumed: false sets session.contextReset to true

Putting { type: 'session_failed', reason: 'model_unknown' } on a thread with a pending user message sets session.state to 'failed' and session.reason to 'model_unknown', and sets that message's status to 'errored' with errorReason 'model_unknown'
After session_started and { type: 'session_closed', reason: 'idle' }, GET /api/projects/web/threads/T by a project VIEWER answers 200 with session.state 'closed' and session.reason 'idle'

routing.reasoning: Extends the established fold with additional line types, one pure helper module, one ack-hook change and a DTO field; patterns are set by US-002/003.

suggestedCriteria: session_closed while session is null sets session with resumed false and contextReset false
A tool_call line whose turnId has no assistant message is counted as a bad line
An ok-acked THREAD_ANSWER for a requestId different from the thread's pendingQuestion.requestId leaves pendingQuestion unchanged
An ok-acked command other than THREAD_ANSWER leaves pendingQuestion unchanged and the existing payload rewrite still happens
outOfScope: Usage and cost arithmetic (US-005); SSE publication (US-006)
US-004 only: `approval_requested` without `callId`, and an `approval_resolved` whose `requestId` matches no entry, change nothing and have no dedicated acceptance criterion.
US-004 only: the 2048-character cut of `pendingQuestion.text` has no dedicated acceptance criterion.

userStories.title: Cost, tokens, budget stops and spend analytics
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fold `usage` lines and the `turn_end` reconcile into message/thread/job cost and tokens plus `FleetCostEvent` rows, signal budgets, and put THREAD jobs under budget hard stops.

**Motivation** — Thread spend is invisible to budgets' hard stops and analytics today, and `ChatThread.costUsd`/`tokens` are never written.

**Approach** (verbatim from spec)
B2-R1 (cost source): usage plus reconcile. Every `usage` line adds its cost and tokens as it arrives. At `turn_end`, the part of `turn_end.costUsd` (and of each `turn_end.usage` token count) above the turn's summed `usage` lines is added as well, so the compaction call that `usage` events leave out is counted. A `turn_end` total at or below the summed usage adds nothing.
B2-R2 (analytics): the fold writes one `FleetCostEvent` row per priced `usage` line, and one per positive `turn_end` reconcile, so every existing spend panel counts thread spend with no query change. Unpriced usage writes no row.

| `usage` | `turnId`, `round` integer, `inputTokens`, `outputTokens` integers >= 0, `costUsd` finite >= 0; optional `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite` integers >= 0, `costSource` one of `computed reported unpriced` |
nax-agent `usage` names its cache fields `cacheRead` / `cacheWrite`, while `turn_end.usage` (`TokenUsage`) names them `cacheReadTokens` / `cacheWriteTokens`.

For a `usage` line, with `cacheRead`/`cacheWrite` absent read as 0:
- tokens: the message's `usage` and the thread's `tokens` (both `{ input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite }`, absent read as zeros) add the line's counts, priced or not, except for a **repeated** priced line: one whose `FleetCostEvent` insert was skipped as a duplicate adds no tokens either. A repeated unpriced line cannot be told apart and is counted;
- priced (`costSource` absent, `computed` or `reported`): insert (skipping a duplicate `(jobId, leaseEpoch, callId)`, so a repeated round never aborts the fold) a `FleetCostEvent` with `jobId`, `leaseEpoch`, `projectId`, `repoId`, `runnerId` from the job; `at` = the line's `at` when it parses as a date, else the fold time; `agentName` = `'native'` for a native backend, else the ACP `agent`; `model` = the thread backend's `model`, else `'default'`; `profile` `'read'`; `stage` `'thread'`; `featureName` = the thread's `feature`; `callId` = `<turnId>:<round>`; the four token counts; `costUsd` = the line's cost; `pricingSource` = `costSource ?? 'computed'`; the message's `costSource` is set to the same value;
- unpriced: no `FleetCostEvent`.

At `turn_end` (B2-R1): the message's summed tokens are compared with `turn_end.usage` (`inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`); each positive difference is added to the message and the thread. If `turn_end.costSource` is not `unpriced` and `turn_end.costUsd` exceeds the sum of the turn's `FleetCostEvent` rows, a `FleetCostEvent` with `callId` `<turnId>:turn_end` and the difference as `costUsd` (token counts 0) is inserted.

Then (B2-D6) `FleetJob.costSpentUsd` = round4(sum of the job's `FleetCostEvent.costUsd` at all epochs), `ChatThread.costUsd` = round4(sum over the thread's THREAD jobs), and each touched message's `costUsd` = round4(sum of the events whose `callId` starts with its `turnId` followed by `:`, matched as a literal prefix). Money is never accumulated by repeated 4-place rounding: the exact per-line cost lives in `FleetCostEvent.costUsd` (8 places); sums are re-derived after each fold and rounded once to 4 places (half-up). All cost comparisons and sums use `Prisma.Decimal`, never floating point. The runner sends no `costSpentUsd` snapshot for a THREAD job (B3b-R4) and no bundle exists, so nothing else writes these.

Budget: after a commit that changed cost, `BudgetEvaluator.signal(jobSpendKeys(job))` (`budget-evaluator.ts:53`; `jobSpendKeys` at `budget-rules.ts:45` gives `global`, `project:<id>`, `repo:<id>`, `runner:<id>`) is called by `ThreadIngestor` (not for a cost-free batch). `BUDGET_STOP_COMMANDS` (`prisma-budget.repository.ts:22`) changes from `[RUN, PLAN]` to `[RUN, PLAN, THREAD]`: a hard stop cancels QUEUED THREAD jobs and requests cancel of held ones through the existing `cancelForBudget`. `windowSpend` already sums every job's `costSpentUsd`. Spend analytics (`prisma-analytics.repository.ts` `spendCells`, `spendTotals`, `jobCostSums`) read only `FleetCostEvent` and need no change. `FleetCostEvent` (`schema.prisma:1248`): unique `(jobId, leaseEpoch, callId)`, `costUsd` Decimal(14,8).

**Scope** — In: thread-cost.ts (event building, reconcile differences, round4), fold of usage/turn_end reconcile, cost re-derivation, budget signal, BUDGET_STOP_COMMANDS. Out: SSE `thread` event publication (US-006), startup catch-up (US-007).

**Interface**
```typescript
// thread-cost.ts (Prisma.Decimal based)
function round4(value: Prisma.Decimal): Prisma.Decimal; // half-up, once
// builds FleetCostEvent create input for a priced usage line and for a turn_end reconcile (callId `<turnId>:turn_end`)
```
acceptanceCriteria: After turn_start t1, putting { type: 'usage', turnId: 't1', round: 1, inputTokens: 100, outputTokens: 20, cacheRead: 5, costUsd: 0.0123 } sets the message's costUsd to '0.0123', costSource to 'computed' and usage deep-equal to { input: 100, output: 20, cacheRead: 5, cacheWrite: 0 }
The same line sets T's costUsd to '0.0123' and tokens deep-equal to { input: 100, output: 20, cacheRead: 5, cacheWrite: 0 }
The same line sets J's costSpentUsd to '0.0123'

The same line creates one FleetCostEvent for J with leaseEpoch 1, callId 't1:1', stage 'thread', agentName 'native', model 'm1', profile 'read', featureName 'add-auth', inputTokens 100, costUsd 0.0123 and pricingSource 'computed'
Ten usage lines (rounds 1 to 10) of costUsd 0.00004 each set J's costSpentUsd to '0.0004' and T's costUsd to '0.0004'
A usage line with costSource 'unpriced', costUsd 0 and inputTokens 50 adds 50 to T's tokens.input, leaves T's costUsd '0' and creates no FleetCostEvent
After usage lines of costUsd 0.01 and 0.02 for t1, putting turn_end (completed) with costUsd 0.05 sets T's costUsd to '0.05' and creates a FleetCostEvent with callId 't1:turn_end' and costUsd 0.02
After usage lines summing 0.03 for t1, a turn_end with costUsd 0.03 creates no FleetCostEvent with callId 't1:turn_end' and leaves T's costUsd '0.03'
After usage lines with inputTokens summing 200 for t1, a turn_end whose usage.inputTokens is 300 sets the message's usage.input and T's tokens.input to 300
Putting the same usage line (t1, round 1, inputTokens 100, costUsd 0.0123) twice in one PUT leaves one FleetCostEvent with callId 't1:1', T's costUsd '0.0123', T's tokens.input 100 and skippedLines 0
With vi.spyOn(app.get(BudgetEvaluator), 'signal'), a PUT containing a priced usage line calls signal with keys including 'global', 'project:<web project id>', 'repo:<repo id>' and 'runner:R'
With the same spy, a PUT containing only turn_start and text_delta lines does not call signal

With a project budget policy { windowKind: 'lifetime', hardStop: true, runningJobs: 'cancel', amountUsd: '0.01' } and a QUEUED THREAD job of a second thread in the project, a priced usage line of costUsd 0.02 for J followed by app.get(BudgetEvaluator).evaluate(policyId, now) moves the QUEUED job to CANCELLED with stateReason 'budget:<policyId>', and J (RUNNING) gets cancelRequestedAt set and one CANCEL command
After a priced usage line of costUsd 0.0123 for J (no at, so inside the default 30-day window), GET /api/projects/web/fleet/analytics/spend by dev answers 200 with totals.costUsd '0.0123'

routing.reasoning: Exact decimal money handling, idempotent cost-event inserts inside the fold transaction, cross-module budget signalling and hard-stop wiring.

suggestedCriteria: round4 rounds half-up: 0.00005 rounds to 0.0001 and 0.00004 rounds to 0
A repeated priced usage line adds no tokens to the message usage
A budget hard stop still cancels a QUEUED RUN job and requests cancel of a held PLAN job after THREAD joins BUDGET_STOP_COMMANDS
outOfScope: Publishing the `thread` SSE event for cost changes (US-006)

US-005 only: `reported` pricing follows the `computed` path without a dedicated acceptance criterion; so do the reconcile of `cacheRead` / `cacheWrite` and `outputTokens` (only `inputTokens` is pinned), and a `turn_end` whose `costSource` is `unpriced`.
US-005 only: the ACP `agentName` and the `'default'` model fallback share the native path without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

userStories.title: Content SSE
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Publish content-carrying thread events after each fold commit and serve them over `GET /projects/:slug/threads/:id/events`.

**Motivation** — B4's chat page needs both the folded rows and a live content feed.

**Approach** (verbatim from spec)
`ThreadEventBus` (`apps/api/src/live/thread-event-bus.ts`): `subscribe(threadId, listener): () => void`, `publish(event: ThreadLiveEvent): void` (routes by `event.threadId`, never throws), same shape as `ProjectEventBus`.

`ThreadLiveEvent` = `{ id: <uuid>, threadId, at }` plus one of:
| `type` | extra fields | published after a batch that |
| `delta` | `messageId`, `text` | appended text to a message and did not reset it; `text` = all text the batch appended to that message |
| `message` | `messageId` | completed a user message (`input_consumed`), created a message, reset it, ended its turn, changed its `toolSummary`, or errored it |
| `question` | `requestId`, `text` | set `pendingQuestion` |
| `thread` | — | changed the thread's `session`, `costUsd`, `tokens` or `pendingQuestion` |

At most one event of each type per message (and one `thread`) per batch, in the order `message`, `delta`, `question`, `thread`. Events go out only after the batch commits. B2-D7: SSE events carry `messageId` (not `id`, which every live event already uses for its own unique id), and `thread` carries no `state`: the client refetches the thread.

`GET /projects/:slug/threads/:id/events` (`ThreadEventsController`, `thread-events.controller.ts`, in `ThreadsModule`, `@Sse()`, `@SkipThrottle()`, `@ApiExcludeEndpoint()`): order of checks: not a user principal -> 403 `threads.principal`; not a project member -> 403 (`assertProjectMembership`); thread not in the project -> 404 `threads.notFound`; no JWT payload -> 403; `LiveStreamRegistry.tryAcquire(userId, maxStreamsPerUser)` false -> 429 (`ThrottleAppException`). Then `createLiveStream({ key: threadId, subscribe: ThreadEventBus.subscribe, stillAllowed: membership re-check as in LiveController, onClose: release })`. Reconnect = refetch messages, then subscribe (B4).

Pattern symbols: `createLiveStream(options)` (`live-stream.ts:31`), `LiveStreamRegistry.tryAcquire / release`, `JwtAuthProvider`, `decodeJwtPayload`, `tokenExpiryMs`, `ILiveConfig` via `LIVE_CFG` (`maxStreamsPerUser` 10, `heartbeatMs`), `LiveController.events` (`live.controller.ts:32-71`).

Module wiring: `LiveModule` also provides `ThreadEventBus` and exports it and `LiveStreamRegistry`; `ThreadsModule` also imports `LiveModule` and `AuthModule` and declares `ThreadEventsController`; `ThreadIngestModule` imports `LiveModule`. The SSE route is excluded from `openapi.json`; `threads.module.spec.ts` assertions stay unchanged.

**Scope** — In: ThreadEventBus, event derivation from fold results, publish after commit in ThreadIngestor, controller and module wiring. Out: B4 client; JWT-expiry/heartbeat behaviour (reused from createLiveStream).

**Interface**
```typescript
type ThreadLiveEvent = { id: string; threadId: string; at: string } & (
  | { type: 'delta'; messageId: string; text: string }
  | { type: 'message'; messageId: string }
  | { type: 'question'; requestId: string; text: string }
  | { type: 'thread' });
class ThreadEventBus { subscribe(threadId: string, listener: (e: ThreadLiveEvent) => void): () => void; publish(event: ThreadLiveEvent): void; }
```
acceptanceCriteria: ThreadEventBus: a listener subscribed for thread 'a' receives an event published with threadId 'a' and does not receive one published with threadId 'b'

With GET /api/projects/web/threads/T/events open as a project VIEWER, putting turn_start t1 and then (in a second PUT) text_delta round 1 'Hi' delivers an event of type 'delta' whose data has threadId T, the message's id as messageId and text 'Hi'
With the stream open, one PUT holding text_delta 'Hel' and text_delta 'lo' for t1 delivers one delta event with text 'Hello' for that message
With the stream open, putting turn_end for t1 delivers a message event whose messageId is the assistant message's id
With the stream open, putting input_consumed for pending user message M delivers a message event with messageId M
With the stream open, one PUT holding text_delta round 1 'abc' and stream_reset round 1 delivers a message event for that message and no delta event for it
With the stream open, putting an answerable question q1 with text 'Which repo?' delivers a question event with requestId 'q1' and text 'Which repo?'
With the stream open, putting session_started delivers a thread event with threadId T
With the stream open, putting a priced usage line delivers a thread event with threadId T
With the stream open on thread T, a PUT for a THREAD job of another thread followed by a session_started PUT for J delivers T's thread event as the first event after 'ready'
GET /api/projects/web/threads/T/events with a rostered agent's API key is refused with 403
GET /api/projects/web/threads/T/events by outsider (no membership) is refused with 403
GET /api/projects/web/threads/<thread of the ops project>/events by root is refused with 404
With 10 live streams of dev already open (project or thread streams), an 11th GET /api/projects/web/threads/T/events by dev is refused with 429

routing.reasoning: New SSE endpoint with principal, membership and stream-limit access control (security-critical), plus event derivation from every fold effect.

suggestedCriteria: ThreadEventBus.publish does not throw when a listener throws
No SSE event is published when the fold transaction rolls back
outOfScope: Thread pages, SSE client and polling fallback (B4)
US-006 only: the JWT expiry close and the heartbeat membership re-check reuse `createLiveStream` unchanged and have no dedicated acceptance criterion.

userStories.title: Startup catch-up and dashboard loads
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Catch up unfolded thread streams at API startup and stop the dashboard from counting THREAD jobs as ordinary runner load.

**Motivation** — A fold that failed on a stream's last append is otherwise never retried, and the dashboard dry-run reports runners as full while they are free for RUN and PLAN work.

**Approach** (verbatim from spec)
`ThreadIngestBootstrap.onApplicationBootstrap()` (`thread-ingest.bootstrap.ts`, in `ThreadIngestModule`) selects THREAD jobs that are non-terminal or have `finishedAt` within the last 24 hours, whose `FleetJobLog` `thread` row (per epoch) has `sizeBytes` greater than that attempt's cursor offset (no cursor = 0), at most 200 attempts ordered by the job's `createdAt` ascending, and awaits `catchUp` for each in that order. A failing `catchUp` is logged and the next job is still caught up. It runs in tests too (an empty database makes it a no-op).

Dashboard: `findHeldRefs` (`IDashboardRepository.findHeldRefs`, `domain/dashboard.domain.ts:15`, `prisma-dashboard.repository.ts:67-73`) changes from `{ runnerId, repoId }[]` to `{ runnerId, repoId, command }[]`, so `toLoads` in `FleetDashboardService.snapshot` classifies THREAD jobs. `toLoads(refs)` (`placement-rules.ts:146-155`) puts a ref whose `command` is `THREAD` into `threads` only; a ref without `command` is counted in `active`. `FleetDashboardService.snapshot` already passes the refs to `toLoads`, so held THREAD jobs leave runners' `activeJobs` and the "queued but not placed" dry-run (`jobUnplaceableItems`, `attention-unplaceable.ts`) no longer treats them as capacity or `busy_repo` load. `jobSilentItems` needs no change: a RUNNING THREAD job heartbeats every 30 s (`threadHeartbeatMs`, B3b) against a 180 s `jobSilentSec`.

Existing test update: `apps/api/test/integration/fleet/fleet-dashboard-repository.integration.spec.ts` — the held-refs assertion `expect(await repo.findHeldRefs()).toEqual([{ runnerId, repoId: web.repoId }])` becomes `toEqual([{ runnerId, repoId: web.repoId, command: 'RUN' }])` (the seeded held job is a RUN job).

Test term: "Written directly" means lines appended with `LogStore.append` at `logKey(job, 1, 'thread')` and a `FleetJobLog` `thread` row with `sizeBytes` equal to the file size, with no cursor.

**Scope** — In: ThreadIngestBootstrap registered in ThreadIngestModule, findHeldRefs command field, updated existing assertion. Out: timer-driven retries; thread-specific dashboard fields or attention rules.

**Interface**
```typescript
class ThreadIngestBootstrap implements OnApplicationBootstrap { onApplicationBootstrap(): Promise<void>; }
// IDashboardRepository.findHeldRefs(): Promise<Array<{ runnerId: string; repoId: string; command: string }>>
```
acceptanceCriteria: For a RUNNING THREAD job J whose stream (turn_start t1, text_delta 'Hi') was written directly, app.get(ThreadIngestBootstrap).onApplicationBootstrap() creates the assistant message with content 'Hi' and a cursor whose offset equals the file size
The same setup for a THREAD job with state COMPLETED and finishedAt 2 hours ago folds its stream
The same setup for a THREAD job with state COMPLETED and finishedAt 3 days ago creates no cursor and no assistant message
With vi.spyOn(app.get(ThreadIngestor), 'catchUp'), onApplicationBootstrap() does not call catchUp for a RUNNING THREAD job whose cursor offset equals its FleetJobLog sizeBytes
With two RUNNING THREAD jobs whose streams were written directly and catchUp spied to reject once for the first, onApplicationBootstrap() resolves and the second job's stream is folded
findHeldRefs() on the booted app's dashboard repository (DASHBOARD_REPOSITORY), while runner R holds a RUNNING THREAD job, returns an entry with runnerId R and command 'THREAD'
GET /api/fleet/dashboard as a global ADMIN while runner R (online, capacity 1) holds only a RUNNING THREAD job answers 200 with R's activeJobs 0
The same request while R holds a RUNNING RUN job and a RUNNING THREAD job answers 200 with R's activeJobs 1

GET /api/fleet/dashboard as a global ADMIN, while R (online, capacity 1, fitting) holds only a RUNNING THREAD job on repo rA and a RUN job on rA has been QUEUED (inserted directly, unplaced) for longer than FLEET_JOB_QUEUED_WARN_SEC, answers 200 with no job_unplaceable attention item for that RUN job

routing.reasoning: One new lifecycle class with a repository query and a small additive change to a dashboard repository return shape; standard patterns.

suggestedCriteria: findHeldRefs() returns command 'RUN' for a held RUN job
onApplicationBootstrap() on an empty database resolves without calling catchUp
The existing fleet-dashboard-repository.integration.spec.ts held-refs assertion passes with command 'RUN' added to the expected entry
outOfScope: The dashboard gains no thread-specific runner field or attention rule.
US-007 only: the `createdAt` order and the 200-attempt bound of the startup catch-up have no dedicated acceptance criterion.

modifiedFiles.reason: the held-refs assertion `expect(await repo.findHeldRefs()).toEqual([{ runnerId, repoId: web.repoId }])` becomes `toEqual([{ runnerId, repoId: web.repoId, command: 'RUN' }])`, because `findHeldRefs` now returns each held job's `command` (the seeded held job is a RUN job). The rows it returns are otherwise unchanged.

analysis:
Feature B2 of fleet S5a phase B. The runner (B3b, #260) ships brainstorm-thread session events as JSONL on a `thread` log stream (PUT /fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/logs/thread); the API refuses it today (400 fleet.logInput). This feature accepts the stream, folds it durably exactly-once into ChatThread/ChatMessage/FleetCostEvent rows, adds a content SSE per thread, puts THREAD jobs under budget hard stops, and fixes dashboard load classification. All work is in apps/api (plus openapi.json regeneration in US-004). Umbrella design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-fleet-s5a-chat-threads-design.md (§2.4, §3.2-3.4).

KEY FILES (verified on main 88686af2 per spec): apps/api/src/fleet/logs/{log-upload.service.ts, log-store.ts, log-read.service.ts, logs.module.ts, domain/fleet-job-log.domain.ts}; apps/api/src/fleet/common/thread-jobs.ts (mirror of package constants; API may only `import type` from packages/fleet-protocol because the image does not ship packages/, protocol.spec.ts pins it); packages/fleet-protocol/src/threads.ts (THREAD_STREAM, THREAD_STREAM_LIMITS, ThreadRunnerLine); apps/api/src/fleet/threads/{prisma-chat-thread.repository.ts (seq allocation SQL ~:166, mapMessage ~:260, messages() ~:71), thread-job-effects.ts, threads.module.ts, threads.service.ts, domain/chat-thread.domain.ts, dto/thread.dto.ts}; apps/api/src/fleet/budgets/{prisma-budget.repository.ts:22, budget-evaluator.ts:53, budget-rules.ts:45}; apps/api/src/fleet/dashboard/{prisma-dashboard.repository.ts:67-73, domain/dashboard.domain.ts:15, dashboard.service.ts}; apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/placement-rules.ts:146-155 (toLoads); apps/api/src/live/{live.controller.ts, live-stream.ts, live-stream-registry.ts, live.module.ts}; apps/api/src/fleet/sync/command-ack.processor.ts (calls onInputAck); apps/api/src/fleet/analytics/prisma-analytics.repository.ts (spend panels read FleetCostEvent only); apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma (FleetCostEvent at ~:1248).

ARCHITECTURE: LogUploadService.upload -> store.withLock(logKey) append -> (lock released) -> LogAppendHooks.run({jobId,leaseEpoch,stream}) -> ThreadIngestor.catchUp (registered by ThreadIngestModule.onModuleInit via a closure that calls this.ingestor.catchUp at call time so vi.spyOn sees it). catchUp takes store.withLock(logKey(...,'thread')) itself (KeyedMutex is in-process and NOT re-entrant: the hook must run after the upload's lock is released). It reads the cursor, scans [offset, min(size, offset+logScanBytes)) up to the last newline, parses lines (thread-line.ts, untrusted), and folds a batch in ONE transaction via ThreadIngestRepository.fold(batch): lock job row then thread row (B1 lock order, job then thread), apply per-line effects (thread-fold.ts), re-derive cost, upsert cursor offset + skippedLines. On fold failure retry one line at a time; a line that still fails is folded as a bad line (B2-D8). After commit publish ThreadEventBus events and BudgetEvaluator.signal(jobSpendKeys(job)) if cost changed. A failing fold never fails the upload (B2-D1).

RULINGS: B2-R1 cost = per-usage-line plus turn_end reconcile of the excess above summed usage; B2-R2 one FleetCostEvent per priced usage line and per positive reconcile (callId `<turnId>:<round>` and `<turnId>:turn_end`); B2-R3 ChatThread.session Json. B2-D2 no in-memory delta buffer; B2-D3 pendingQuestion cleared on THREAD_ANSWER ok-ack, turn_end, and job end (B1); B2-D4 informational question -> toolSummary entry ask_human; B2-D5 raw thread stream never served by job-log routes (list omits, entries/raw 404 fleet.logs, no fleet_log live event); B2-D6 money never accumulated by repeated rounding: exact sums of FleetCostEvent.costUsd (14,8) re-derived after each fold, round4 half-up once, all with Prisma.Decimal; B2-D7 SSE events carry messageId (not id) and `thread` events carry no state; B2-D8 line-by-line retry.

MIGRATION: new migration apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261014090000_thread_ingest/migration.sql adds ThreadIngestCursor (PK jobId+leaseEpoch, FK to FleetJob ON DELETE CASCADE), ChatThread.session jsonb null, ChatMessage.streamRound / streamRoundStart int null. Integration suites build their schema from schema.prisma. Existing rows must be unaffected (session stays null).

RISKS: (1) Non-reentrant KeyedMutex deadlock if the hook runs inside the upload lock. (2) Lock-order inversions: always job row then thread row. (3) NUL chars in strings must be replaced with U+FFFD before any DB write. (4) mapMessage must hide the fold-internal streamRound columns from list and send payloads. (5) logKey/isUploadStream widening must not leak `thread` into LogReadService/LogFallbackService/LiveFleetLogEvent (keep narrow LogStreamName; isLogStream('thread') stays false). (6) Existing fleet-dashboard-repository.integration.spec.ts held-refs assertion must gain command: 'RUN'. (7) ThreadsModule gains LiveModule and AuthModule imports; threads.module.spec.ts compiles with stubs and must keep passing. (8) Cost comparisons must use Prisma.Decimal not floats. (9) Do not edit generated files; regenerate openapi.json with `bun run api:export-spec` in US-004. (10) Test conventions: unit tests src/**/*.spec.ts, integration under apps/api/test/integration/**; do not create us-XXX folders. Integration for apps/api needs the test Postgres (`bun run test:db:up` in apps/api).

STORY ORDER: US-001 (stream acceptance, hook, schema, fixtures) -> US-002 (ingestor engine, parser, cursor) -> US-003 (assistant lifecycle) -> US-004 (tools/questions/session, ack clear, DTO) -> US-005 (cost, budgets, analytics) -> US-006 (SSE) -> US-007 (bootstrap + dashboard). The structure is binding.
outOfScope: Thread pages, composables, the SSE client and polling fallback, and rendering `session`, tool chips and question cards belong to feature `fleet-s5a-thread-web` (B4).
`write_doc` and `published` / `publish_failed` lines, Publish, Plan and Run from a thread belong to phase C; until then those line types are counted as bad lines.
ACP backends (phase D): the fold handles their lines identically; no ACP-specific behaviour is added.
The API clamp for a negative remaining `maxCostUsd` at dispatch (a B1 follow-up) is not part of this feature.
Unpriced usage adds no `FleetCostEvent`, so analytics token totals omit unpriced tokens; the thread's own `tokens` include them.
`thinking_delta` and `compaction` lines stay only in the raw stream; nothing renders reasoning text.
A thread stream left unfolded until log retention deletes it (30 days after the job ended) loses the unfolded lines; every append and every startup retries the fold first.
A line with no newline within `FLEET_LOG_SCAN_BYTES` stalls that stream's fold; the runner caps lines at 64 KiB and the scan window is at least 64 KiB.
The fold assumes a single API instance (`KeyedMutex` is in-process), as the rest of fleet logs does.
The API does not check `pendingQuestion.expiresAt`; an expired question clears at the next `turn_end` or job end.
Analytics job panels (`topJobs`, finish results, escalation reasons) keep excluding THREAD jobs (`NAX_JOBS`); only spend panels count them.
The dashboard gains no thread-specific runner field or attention rule.
Spend analytics `totals.jobs` and `medianJobCostUsd` count THREAD jobs once their cost events exist; that is intended, since they read the same cost-event table.
A fold that fails on a stream's last append is retried only at the next append or the next API start; there is no timer-driven retry.

Per-type field-rule failures other than those pinned (a non-integer `round`, a negative token count, a `question.expiresAt` that is not a date, a missing `turnId`) share the line validation without a dedicated acceptance criterion in the story that adds each line type.
US-001 only: `GET .../logs/thread/raw` and the download route share the `thread` refusal of the entries route; only entries is pinned.

US-002 only: two catch-ups of one stream are serialized by the stream's `withLock` key and the fold transaction locks the job row, then the thread row (B1 order); no acceptance criterion races two uploads or an upload against a job end.

The fold stores text as the runner redacted it (`redactSecrets` on deltas, output and error messages; nax-agent's best-effort redaction of tool inputs and previews); the API adds no redaction of its own.
US-003 only: `turn_end` with `outputTruncated: true` keeps the streamed text without a dedicated acceptance criterion; it follows the same "content unchanged" rule as a non-completed turn.
US-002 only: per-type length bounds (`turnId`, `messageId`, `callId`, `name`, `requestId`, `reason`, `decidedBy`) share the line validation without a dedicated acceptance criterion.
US-004 only: `approval_requested` without `callId`, and an `approval_resolved` whose `requestId` matches no entry, change nothing and have no dedicated acceptance criterion.
US-004 only: the 2048-character cut of `pendingQuestion.text` has no dedicated acceptance criterion.

US-005 only: `reported` pricing follows the `computed` path without a dedicated acceptance criterion; so do the reconcile of `cacheRead` / `cacheWrite` and `outputTokens` (only `inputTokens` is pinned), and a `turn_end` whose `costSource` is `unpriced`.
US-005 only: the ACP `agentName` and the `'default'` model fallback share the native path without a dedicated acceptance criterion.
US-006 only: the JWT expiry close and the heartbeat membership re-check reuse `createLiveStream` unchanged and have no dedicated acceptance criterion.
